Predicates:
Visited(x, y) ::: x visited y.
MountainRange(y) ::: y is a mountain range.
LocatedIn(y, z) ::: y is located in z.
Donated(x) ::: x was donated.
Mine(x) ::: x is a mine.
In(z, y) ::: z is in y.
InRegion(y, z) ::: y is in region z.
HasMine(y) ::: y has a mine.
Donated(y) ::: y is donated.
Region(z) ::: z is a region.
InRegion(y, z) ::: y is in region z.
MineIn(y, z) ::: mine y is in region z.
Donated(y) ::: mine y is donated.

Premises:
MountainRange(piruris) ∧ InRegion(piruris, NM ∨ TX) ::: The Picuris Mountains are a mountain range in New Mexico or Texas.
Visited(juan, piruris) ::: Juan de Onate visited the Picuris Mountains.
Mine(pegmatiteMine) ∧ LocatedIn(pegmatiteMine, piruris) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine is located in the Picuris Mountains.
Donated(pegmatiteMine) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine was donated.
InRegion(piruris, TX) → ∀x (MineIn(x, TX) ∧ Donated(x)) → false ::: There are no mountain ranges in Texas that have mines which have been donated.

Conclusion:
Visited(juan, piruris) ∧ InRegion(piruris, NM) ::: Juan de Onate visited a mountain range in New Mexico.
